title: Doom is a Tony Stark variant
claim: Robert Downey Jr.'s Doom is Tony Stark from another universe: a Tony who never had the cave, Pepper or Morgan, and turned his genius toward control instead.

evidence.text: Robert Downey Jr., who played Tony Stark, is announced as Victor von Doom.
evidence.citation: San Diego Comic-Con, Hall H, 27 July 2024

evidence.text: Tony Stark dies in the 616 universe.
Variants of one person can look identical yet live completely different lives.

against: Marvel announced him as Victor von Doom, not as a Stark.
Many fans want a classic Doom; a Stark twist would undercut the character.

title: Doom is holding 616 together with Tony
claim: Tony Stark was the anchor that held the main universe together. Since his death, Doom has used science and sorcery to keep that anchor 'alive', and so keep Earth-616 from fading.

evidence.text: Some people are anchor beings: when they die, their universe slowly dies too.
Tony Stark dies after the snap.

against: Nothing on screen links Doom to Tony's body.
No film has said who Earth-616's anchor is.

title: Steve's happy ending broke the timeline
claim: When Steve stayed in the past with Peggy, he didn't just retire: he cracked reality. That fracture is what lets Doom in, and why Steve is pulled back now.

evidence.text: Steve stays in the past and lives his life with Peggy.
Chris Evans returns as Steve Rogers.

against: Endgame explains that changing the past creates a new branch rather than breaking the old one.
Marvel hasn't connected Steve's choice to the incursions.

title: Franklin gave Doom his face
claim: In the nursery, Doom has the infant Franklin touch his scarred face. Franklin's reality-bending power remakes it, and Doom chooses a face the heroes already trust.

evidence.text: A hooded figure with a Doom mask sits with young Franklin; the face is never shown.
evidence.citation: The Fantastic Four: First Steps, post-credits scene

evidence.text: In the comics, Franklin Richards can reshape reality.

against: The scene shows no powers being used.
It's a large leap from one quiet scene.

title: Franklin is the key to everything
claim: Doom isn't after the heroes; he's after Franklin. And in the end, Franklin could be the one who rebuilds the multiverse, giving the MCU a fresh start after Secret Wars.

evidence.text: Franklin is born, and Galactus wants him for his power.
Doom is seen with Franklin.
evidence.citation: The Fantastic Four: First Steps, post-credits scene

against: A full reset seems more likely in Secret Wars than in Doomsday.
Franklin's role in Doomsday hasn't been revealed.

title: Doom, not the Fantastic Four, flew that ship
claim: The ship bearing the Fantastic Four's emblem that arrives on Earth-616 may not carry the family at all, but Doom in a stolen ship, or Franklin sent away for safety.

evidence.text: A ship from another dimension, matching the Fantastic Four's, arrives on Earth-616 as the New Avengers watch.
The Fantastic Four meet Steve Rogers.
evidence.citation: Final trailer, as reported by Variety

against: The trailer puts the Fantastic Four themselves on Earth-616.
First Steps ends with the family together at home.

title: Doom thinks he's the hero
claim: Like Thanos in Infinity War, Doom drives the story. He believes the universes must be saved, even if that means ruling them, and he'll make the heroes look like the problem.

evidence.text: Doom tells the heroes they have all lived 'stolen lives'.
evidence.citation: Final trailer, as reported by The Hollywood Reporter

evidence.text: The directors' last villain, Thanos, was the protagonist of his film.

against: Doom is still pitched as the threat to all three universes.
A Thanos rerun risks feeling familiar.

title: The Ten Rings are a door to the Beyonders
claim: The Ten Rings are signalling something far away. In the comics, Doom gains godlike power from the cosmic Beyonders, and the rings may be how he finds them.

evidence.text: The Ten Rings send a signal to somewhere unknown.
evidence.citation: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings, mid-credits scene

evidence.text: Simu Liu's Shang-Chi is in the Doomsday cast.
Doom takes the Beyonders' power to build Battleworld.

against: Marvel has never said what the signal reaches.
The Beyonders haven't appeared in the MCU.

title: Battleworld begins in Doomsday
claim: As the universes collide, Doom stitches the survivors into one patchwork planet with himself as god-emperor. Some fans think he uses the Scarlet Witch's chaos magic to do it.

evidence.text: When universes collide, one is destroyed.
evidence.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

evidence.text: Doomsday's heroes come from three distinct universes.
Doom rules Battleworld, built from the remains of dead universes.

against: The Scarlet Witch isn't in Marvel's official cast list.
Battleworld may be saved for Secret Wars.

title: Earth-616 has its own secret council
claim: Somewhere on our Earth, a hidden group of geniuses has been making universe-sized decisions without telling anyone, and Doomsday drags them into the light. Some go further: a council of Reed Richards variants.

evidence.text: Earth-838 is run by a secret council, the Illuminati, including a Reed Richards.
evidence.citation: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness

evidence.text: Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards is in Doomsday.

against: No 616 Illuminati has been teased.
The 838 Illuminati were wiped out by Wanda.

title: This Steve isn't on our side
claim: The Steve Rogers who returns could be a dark variant (even a Hydra Captain America) in a team of evil Avengers that Doom leads against the heroes.

evidence.text: Chris Evans returns as Steve Rogers.
In the comics, a reality-altered Steve Rogers is revealed as a Hydra agent.

against: Everything shown so far is about Steve's family, not betrayal.
The Fantastic Four seek him out for help.

title: The missing heroes are hidden, not gone
claim: Doctor Strange, the Scarlet Witch, the Hulk and Spider-Man aren't on the cast list because Marvel is hiding them, either as surprise returns or because they've already fallen before the film begins.

evidence.text: Doctor Strange, the Scarlet Witch and the Hulk are not in Marvel's official Doomsday cast list.
Marvel has kept major returns off cast lists before.

against: Absent from a cast list may simply mean absent from the film.

title: The X-Men and Avengers fight first
claim: The first meeting of the Fox X-Men and the Avengers won't be friendly. Two worlds on a collision course means two teams with every reason to fight, just as in the comics' Secret Wars.

evidence.text: The Avengers, X-Men and Fantastic Four appear together for the first time.
Patrick Stewart, Ian McKellen and James Marsden return as Xavier, Magneto and Cyclops.

against: Doom is a shared enemy, which pushes the teams together.
A House of M version is probably too much for one film.

title: The Avengers lose on purpose
claim: The wildest one: one of the smartest heroes (Strange, or Reed) decides Doom's plan prevents something worse and lets him win. Secret Wars becomes a reckoning, not revenge.

evidence.text: Doctor Strange has made world-altering choices alone before.
evidence.citation: Spider-Man: No Way Home; Multiverse of Madness

against: There's no footage or announcement pointing this way.
Strange isn't in the official cast list.
